section: Germany: partners' profit shares and the year of moving to or from Germany, tax year 2026
wording: This skill covers two gaps the other Germany skills leave open. Part 1 is the partner in a partnership: how the partnership's profit is fixed once for all partners and then taxed in each partner's own return. Part 2 is the person who moves to or from Germany during 2026: one assessment as a resident for the whole year, with the foreign income of the other months raising the tax rate.

wording: **Part 1, partners.**
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **In scope.** A person resident in Germany (§ 1(1) EStG) who is a co-entrepreneur (Mitunternehmer) of a partnership: a partner in an OHG, a KG (general or limited partner), a GmbH & Co. KG, a GbR or a PartG that runs a business or a profession. Their income is "die Gewinnanteile der Gesellschafter ... und die Vergütungen, die der Gesellschafter von der Gesellschaft für seine Tätigkeit im Dienst der Gesellschaft oder für die Hingabe von Darlehen oder für die Überlassung von Wirtschaftsgütern bezogen hat" (§ 15(1) sentence 1 no. 2 EStG). A partner holding through another partnership is treated the same way (§ 15(1) sentence 1 no. 2 sentence 2).
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Trade or profession.** A partnership whose partners all practise a free profession (§ 18(1) no. 1 EStG: doctors, lawyers, engineers, architects, tax advisers and the like) has income from self-employed work; § 18(4) applies § 15(1) no. 2 and § 15a to it, so the same profit share and Sondervergütung rules apply. It pays no trade tax unless one of two rules makes the whole activity a trade:
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Abfärbung (§ 15(3) no. 1 EStG).** A separable own commercial activity can make the whole activity commercial, subject to the two-gate de minimis exception below, whether that branch makes a profit or a loss. Commercial participation income is a separate limb without that de minimis exception. Its trade-tax treatment follows the separate route in `de-trade-tax`.
disposition: Bounded DE-R01–08 wording/evidence successor

wording: - **Gewerbliche Prägung (§ 15(3) no. 2 EStG).** A partnership with no commercial activity whose only personally liable partners are capital companies, managed only by them or by non-partners. A GmbH & Co. KG run by its GmbH is the usual case.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Out of scope.** Partnerships that opted to be taxed as a company (§ 1a KStG); partners that are companies (de-corporate-tax); sale or closing of a partnership share (§§ 16, 34 EStG); a change of partners during the year; foreign partnerships. Refer.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: **Part 2, the year of moving.**
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **In scope.** An individual who, in 2026, takes up or gives up a German home or habitual abode, so that they are fully liable for part of the year and either limited liable or not liable at all for the rest. Arrivals and departures alike.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **The rule.** Income tax is an annual tax, assessed per calendar year (§ 2(7) sentences 1 and 2 EStG). "Besteht während eines Kalenderjahres sowohl unbeschränkte als auch beschränkte Einkommensteuerpflicht, so sind die während der beschränkten Einkommensteuerpflicht erzielten inländischen Einkünfte in eine Veranlagung zur unbeschränkten Einkommensteuerpflicht einzubeziehen" (§ 2(7) sentence 3). So there is one assessment as a resident, covering the whole year.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Out of scope.** The exit tax on shares when leaving (leaving-germany-exit-tax); a person who never becomes resident (de-non-resident-tax); the extended limited liability under § 2 AStG.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: **Step 1: the partnership's profit is fixed once.** Where several people share in income, it is fixed separately and uniformly for all of them (§ 180(1) sentence 1 no. 2 (a) AO; § 179(2) AO). The determination notice (Feststellungsbescheid) binds each partner's own assessment. It fixes:
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: 1. **The partnership's own profit** (Gesamthandsgewinn), from its books or cash accounts. Trade tax is not deductible (§ 4(5b) EStG).
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: 2. **Each partner's Sondervergütungen**: pay for work for the partnership, interest on loans to it, rent for assets let to it (§ 15(1) no. 2 EStG). If the partnership booked them as costs, they are added back to that partner. They are business income, not wages, interest or rent.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: 3. **Each partner's special business income and costs** (Sonderbetriebseinnahmen and -ausgaben): for example interest on a loan the partner took to buy the share, or the partner's own costs on a building let to the partnership. Each partner reports these to the partnership so they go into the determination.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: 4. **The split.** Profit share by the partnership agreement, plus the partner's own items from 2 and 3.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: 5. **Other items**: income exempt under a treaty that matters for the partners' rate (§ 180(5) no. 1 AO), and tax withheld to be credited (§ 180(5) no. 2 AO); for a commercial partnership, the § 35 figures (Step 3).
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: **Step 2: the partner's own return.** The partner takes the determined share into their own return as business income (trade or self-employed), adds any other income, and from there follows de-income-tax: special expenses, tariff, surcharge, church tax. The partner does not recompute the share; if it is wrong, the determination notice is what gets challenged.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: **Step 3: trade tax and the § 35 credit.** A commercial partnership pays trade tax itself (§ 5 GewStG; see de-trade-tax). Its trade income starts from the profit fixed in Step 1, Sondervergütungen and special items included (§ 7 GewStG). A partner's share of profit from another partnership is taken out again (§ 9 no. 2 GewStG), because that partnership pays its own trade tax. The base amount, the trade tax actually payable and each partner's share of both are fixed in the same determination (§ 35(2) sentence 1 and (4) EStG). Each partner's share follows the general profit-sharing key, ignoring advance shares (§ 35(2) sentence 2). The BMF letter on § 35 says the same for Sondervergütungen and for results of special and supplementary balance sheets (BMF 3 November 2016, Rn. 22), and a partner that cannot use the credit, such as a GmbH general partner, still takes its key share (Rn. 24). A managing partner's Sondervergütung therefore gives no extra credit. The partner's credit is the lowest of: 4 × share of the base amount; the tax on trade income in the partner's own return (positive trade income / all positive income × tariff tax, § 35(1) sentence 2); the share of trade tax actually payable. Unused credit is lost.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: **Step 4: losses of limited partners (§ 15a EStG).** A limited partner's loss share cannot be set against other income, or carried back or forward under § 10d, so far as it creates or increases a negative capital account. Exception: losses up to the amount by which the registered liability exceeds the contribution actually paid, if the partner is entered in the commercial register, the liability is proven, and a claim under it is not excluded by contract or unlikely (§ 15a(1) sentences 2 and 3). The blocked loss is only set against later profits from the same partnership (§ 15a(2)). It is fixed each year in a separate notice (§ 15a(4)). Withdrawals that create or increase a negative capital account are added as profit only to the extent they are not covered by qualifying outside liability that exists or arises because of those withdrawals under § 15a(1) sentence 2, subject to its register, proof and genuine-exposure conditions. The add-back is capped at the losses deductible in that year and the ten years before (§ 15a(3)). The same rule applies to atypical silent partners and to GbR partners whose liability is excluded or unlikely (§ 15a(5)).
disposition: Bounded DE-R01–08 wording/evidence successor

wording: **Step 5: the retained-profits option (§ 34a EStG), in summary.** A partner whose profit is computed from balance sheets (§ 4(1) or § 5) and whose share is over 10% or over EUR 10,000 may apply, per partnership share and per year, for profit left in the business to be taxed at 28.25% in 2026 instead of the tariff. Profit left in = profit less the positive balance of withdrawals over contributions, plus trade tax (§ 34a(2)). Exclude withdrawals for the income tax under § 34a(1) sentence 1 and its related solidarity surcharge; withdrawals are deemed used first for these taxes up to their amount (§ 34a(2) sentences 2–3). When later withdrawals exceed later profits, the amount fixed as liable to recapture is taxed at 25% (§ 34a(4)). The surcharge applies to both. The calculation is not set out here: refer.
disposition: Bounded DE-R01–08 wording/evidence successor

wording: **Step 1: split the year.** Fix the date the German home or habitual abode began or ended. The months before arrival or after departure are the "other period".
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: **Step 2: the taxable base.** It contains:
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - all income of the resident months, worldwide (§ 2(1) EStG: income earned "während seiner unbeschränkten Einkommensteuerpflicht");
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - German-source income of the other period (§ 49 EStG; see de-non-resident-tax), for example rent from a German flat let before arrival (§ 2(7) sentence 3);
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - the full basic allowance and the full employee lump sum: there is no cut by months for a resident assessment. Special expenses of the resident months are deducted as usual; for contributions paid in the other months see Cross-border points.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: **Step 3: income that raises the rate.** These are left out of the base but added to find the rate (§ 32b(1) sentence 1):
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **No. 2: foreign income of the other period** that was not subject to German tax ("ausländische Einkünfte, die im Veranlagungszeitraum nicht der deutschen Einkommensteuer unterlegen haben"), for cases of part-year full liability, including § 2(7) sentence 3 cases. The official guidance confirms: on arrival or departure, income earned outside the period of full liability counts for the progression clause if it is not subject to limited liability (EStH 2025, H 32b "Zeitweise unbeschränkte Steuerpflicht").
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **No. 3: income a tax treaty exempts in Germany**, in the resident months (often foreign employment income or foreign rent).
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: **Exception for EU and EEA items under no. 3 only (§ 32b(1) sentence 2).** Treaty-exempt rent from property in another EU or EEA state, profits of an EU or EEA farm, and profits of an EU or EEA commercial establishment that fails the active-business test of § 2a(2), do not raise the rate. The exception is written for no. 3 only. Foreign rent of the months before arrival falls under no. 2 and raises the rate wherever the property is.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: **Step 4: the amount added (§ 32b(2)).** Foreign income is computed under German rules: profit or surplus, not gross receipts. For foreign pay, the EUR 1,230 employee lump sum is deducted only to the extent it was not already deducted against German pay, and actual Werbungskosten only so far as all Werbungskosten together exceed the lump sum (§ 32b(2) sentence 2 (a) and (b)). Extraordinary income in it counts at one fifth. Foreign losses lower the rate and can bring it to zero (EStH 2025, H 32b "Ausländische Verluste"). Contributions to the Swiss AHV do not reduce the amount added (same, citing BFH 18 April 2012).
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: **Step 5: the tax.** Tariff tax on (taxable income + amount added), divided by that sum, cut to four decimal places of a percent = special rate. Special rate × taxable income, rounded down = income tax. Then the surcharge and church tax on that tax (de-income-tax).
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: **Joint assessment in the year of moving.** Spouses may choose it if both were fully liable and not permanently separated at some time in the year (§ 26(1) EStG). If both move together, the year qualifies.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Late partnership return (§ 152(6) and (7) AO).** The late-filing surcharge rules for tax returns apply. Amount: 0.0625% of the positive sum of the determined income for each started month late, at least EUR 25 a month, rounded down to whole euros, at most EUR 25,000 (§ 152(10) AO). It must be set if the return is not filed within 14 months after the end of the year (for 2026: by 29 February 2028), unless the deadline was extended (§ 152(2) and (3) no. 1 AO, applied by § 152(6)). The nil-tax let-outs of § 152(3) nos. 2 and 3 do not apply to this return. It is set first against the partnership if it has legal capacity (§ 152(4) sentence 3 AO).
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Partner's own return.** Late filing, interest (0.15% a month from 1 April 2028) and late payment: see de-income-tax.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Interest is charged on the partner, not the partnership.** The determination sets no tax, so § 233a AO interest runs only on each partner's income tax.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Wrong figures.** Tax evasion (§ 370 AO) and reckless understatement (§ 378 AO): refer.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Foreign partner in a German partnership.** A non-resident partner of a German commercial partnership has German income from a permanent establishment (§ 49(1) no. 2 (a) EStG): de-non-resident-tax. The determination is still made (§ 180(3) no. 1 AO excludes it only where just one partner is liable in Germany).
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **German partner in a foreign partnership.** Treaty-exempt profit is still determined where it matters for the partners' rate (§ 180(5) no. 1 AO) and raises the rate under § 32b(1) no. 3, with the EU/EEA exception for establishments that fail the active-business test.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Leaving Germany with a partnership share.** A partner's share is business property. Leaving the country can be a deemed withdrawal or a trigger under leaving-germany-exit-tax, which also names a limited partner with more than 25% of the income as having a substantial interest. Refer before the move.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Arrival with foreign pay or rent.** Use Part 2. Foreign tax paid on income of the other period gives no credit in Germany, because Germany does not tax that income; it only raises the rate.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Social security.** Contributions linked to pay that a treaty exempts in Germany (the § 32b(1) no. 3 case) are not special expenses (§ 10(2) sentence 1 no. 1 EStG; BMF letter on Vorsorgeaufwendungen, Rn. 199), unless the pay was earned in an EU or EEA state or Switzerland and that state allows no deduction for them (§ 10(2) sentence 1 no. 1 (a) to (c)). Contributions on foreign pay of the months before arrival or after departure (the no. 2 case) are not settled here (see Not yet confirmed). Swiss AHV contributions do not reduce the amount added for the rate (H 32b). Social security itself: de-social-contributions.
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

section: Example 1: managing limited partner of a GmbH & Co. KG
wording: The Alpha GmbH & Co. KG runs a wholesale business in a town with a trade tax multiplier of 380%. Its general partner is a GmbH with no share in profit. Two limited partners: Anna (60%) and Ben (40%). In 2026 the KG's own profit, after booking Anna's management pay as a cost and before trade tax, is EUR 300,000. Anna's management pay from the KG: EUR 120,000 (a Sondervergütung). Anna pays EUR 4,000 interest on a loan she took to buy her share (a Sonderbetriebsausgabe). No trade tax add-backs or reductions. Anna is single, no church, no other income, and her deductible insurance is EUR 15,000. (Invented case; the multiplier is an input.)

section: Example 2: arrival on 1 July 2026 with foreign pay for January to June
wording: Clara moves from London to Munich on 1 July 2026 and takes a job there. January to June she earned EUR 30,000 (converted) from her UK employer; she had no German income in those months. July to December she earns EUR 36,000 gross in Germany. Her Werbungskosten are below the lump sum. Deductible insurance for her German months, from the certificates: EUR 5,500. Single, no church, no other income. (Invented case.)

section: DE-R01–08 added ordinary method / intake / selected source
wording: **Separable own commercial side activity: annual net-receipt test.** Under the BFH interpretation adopted in BMF EStH 2025 H 15.8(5), an otherwise noncommercial partnership's separable own commercial activity does not reclassify the rest if BOTH `commercial net receipts ≤ 0.03 × total partnership net receipts` AND `commercial net receipts ≤ EUR 24,500` for the assessment period. Total receipts include the commercial and noncommercial activities, excluding VAT. Apply the same test whether the commercial branch makes a profit or a loss. The branch remains commercial in its own right; an inseparably commercial overall activity does not become a free profession under this exception. This own-activity test does not apply to commercial income received through a participation in another partnership; keep that income-tax limb and its separate trade-tax treatment distinct.

section: DE-R01–08 added ordinary method / intake / selected source
wording: For an otherwise qualifying separable professional partnership, total net receipts of EUR 500,000 and commercial net receipts of EUR 15,000 pass both gates exactly; EUR 15,000.01 fails the 3% gate. At total net receipts of EUR 1,000,000, commercial receipts of EUR 24,500 pass both; EUR 24,500.01 fails the absolute gate although below 3%. These are receipts tests, not a profit allowance. The outcome under these two gates is unchanged if the commercial branch has a loss.
